text:
sam: Kicking off a feature-swap for model-route service: v3 -> v4. Plan: 5% -> 20% after 10m -> 50% after 20m. Change window 02:00-03:00 UTC (09:00 PT).

maya: Copy. Who's owning metrics/watch? I'll take latency and error-rate.

jin: I can watch throughput and downstream queueing. Will set up quick dashboards.

deploybot: [deploybot] scheduled traffic-shift job created: job_id=fs-6901, target=v4, initial=5%, ramp=[10m->20%,20m->50%].

sam: Ops: please be ready to pin back to v3 if 95th P95 latency spikes > 200ms or errors +3% above baseline.

ops: Roger. I'll keep the emergency rollback playbook handy. Ping me with `!pin v3` in this thread to trigger immediate drain.

maya: Added a quick smoke prompt set to the Canary runbook, will run every 5m. If content-quality drift > 2% we halt.

jin: Dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/srv/model-route?orgId=1&from=now-30m&to=now - pinned important panels.

sam: deploybot, start the job now.

deploybot: [deploybot] starting traffic shift for job_id=fs-6901 -> current traffic to v4=5% at 02:05:45 UTC.

maya: Smoke run #1: pass. latency +6ms, errors flat.

jin: Observed slight increase in KV cache miss on edge nodes (+1.2%). Not concerning yet.

sam: After 10m we'll move to 20%. If any red signals appear before that we abort.

deploybot: [deploybot] automated ramp to 20% executed at 02:15:50 UTC. current traffic to v4=20%.

ops: Noted a small spike in 500s on svc-auth around 02:16 but it resolved quickly. No action taken.

maya: Smoke run #2: content-quality diff = 0.8% (within threshold).

jin: Throughput steady, downstream queue depth +4% but within SLA.

sam: Proceed to 50% now if everyone thumbs up.

ops: Thumbs up from ops.

maya: +1 from QA.

deploybot: [deploybot] executing ramp to 50% for job_id=fs-6901. ETA for completion 02:26:30 UTC.

deploybot: [deploybot] ramp complete. current traffic to v4=50%.

sam: Monitoring 10m after final ramp. If we hit any of these triggers: latency P95 >200ms, error-rate +3%, content drift >2% -> we pin.

jin: Noticed a flurry of 429s on a subset of queries at 02:28. Suspecting client-side retries. Pulling request traces now.

maya: Smoke run #3: pass but one test flaked (timeout 3s -> 5s).

ops: I'm on-call and stand by to pin. We should decide by 02:35 UTC if flake persists.

sam: If it's only one flaky test and it doesn't affect user-facing errors, hold. But if user-facing errors increase, we pin.

jin: Traces show high latency from one edge region (eu-west-2) caused by an overloaded forwarder. I'll open an infra incident, tagging @netops.

ops: If you want a quick rollback instead of partial network fix, say so. Pin back would be immediate drain from v4 to v3.

sam: Hold on a sec — give network a 5m window. If region doesn't recover by 02:40 we pin.

deploybot: [deploybot] note: you can run `!pin v3 --job fs-6901 --reason "roll back due to eu-west-2 forwarder"` to trigger immediate pin and traffic drain.

maya: Acknowledge. QA will keep running smoke every 2m.

jin: netops responded, started rolling capacity in eu-west-2 at 02:31. Latency trending down.

ops: Thanks. Stand down on pin for now.

sam: Good call. Continue 50% soak for another 15m, then we'll schedule full cutover during low traffic window tomorrow.

deploybot: [deploybot] job_id=fs-6901 remains at 50% soak. Next automated checkpoint in 15m.

maya: I'll capture notes for release: "feature-swap model-route v4: ramped to 50% on 2026-03-22 02:05 UTC; minor eu-west-2 transient; no rollback; follow-up: capacity increase for forwarder in eu-west-2."

sam: Thanks all. If anything urgent, ping @ops and drop `!pin` command.

ops: Acknowledged. :thumbsup:
